actual_primary_readings.finding: Publisher distinguishes Coastal LiDAR Study, Sediment Transport Study and Shoreline Change Study among CRMP technical components. The page has no linked final SCS report or exact source-image epochs.

SCS mapped historical shoreline positions and classified segments by geomorphic behavior. LiDAR supplied topography, bathymetry and aerial photography for subsequent analyses. Cliff investigations and probabilistic hazards were separate activities. The SCS link46 and LiDAR link41 are same-page section anchors, not downloadable study bodies. Programme2012–2020 is not imagery acquisition range.
Bibliography is grouped with Annexes, rather than the PartA/PartD files already read. Stopped annex target was not retried.

Printed35 attributes coastal stability discussion to CRMP Shoreline Change Study (Baird2015c); FigureA21 cites Baird2015. Printed59 also uses Baird2015c for2015LiDAR. This unresolved short-citation ambiguity does not license treating the two studies as one or assigning2015 to every shoreline position. Historical shoreline extrema for erosion hazards and cliff aerial-comparison methods belong to different analytical contexts.
